b.ab736f7f08:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.49d19a82a7:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro secúndo Machabæórum
<r>2 Mac 3:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Igitur, cum sancta cívitas habitarétur in omni pace, leges étiam adhuc óptime custodiréntur, propter Oníæ pontíficis pietátem, et ánimos ódio habéntes mala,
<n>2</n> Fiébat ut et ipsi reges et príncipes locum summo honóre dignum dúcerent, et templum máximis munéribus illustrárent:
<n>3</n> Ita ut Seléucus Asiæ rex de reddítibus suis præstáret omnes sumptus ad ministérium sacrificiórum pertinéntes.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Dixit Iudas Simóni fratri suo: Elige tibi viros et vade, líbera fratres tuos in Galilǽam; ego autem et Iónathas frater tuus íbimus in Galaadítim:
* Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.
<r>℣.</r> Accingímini, fílii poténtes, et estóte paráti: quóniam mélius est nobis, mori in bello, quam vidére mala gentis nostræ et sanctórum.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut fúerit volúntas in cælo, sic fiat.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the second book of Machabees
<r>2 Mac 3:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Therefore when the holy city was inhabited with all peace, and the laws as yet were very well kept, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and the hatred his soul had of evil,
<n>2</n> It came to pass that even the kings themselves, and the princes esteemed the place worthy of the highest honour, and glorified the temple with very great gifts:
<n>3</n> So that Seleucus king of Asia allowed out of his revenues all the charges belonging to the ministry of the sacrifices.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Judas said unto Simon his brother: Choose thee out men, and go, and deliver thy brethren that are in Galilee and I, and Jonathan thy brother, will go into the country of Galaad.
* As the Will is in heaven, so let it be.
<r>℣.</r> Arm yourselves, ye valiant men, and be in readiness for it is better for us to die in battle, than to behold the calamities of our people, and our sanctuary.
<r>℟.</r> As the Will is in heaven, so let it be.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>2 Mac 3:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> Simon autem de tribu Béniamin, præpósitus templi constitútus, contendébat, obsisténte sibi príncipe sacerdótum, iníquum áliquid in civitáte molíri.
<n>5</n> Sed, cum víncere Oníam non posset, venit ad Apollónium Tharsǽæ fílium, qui eo témpore erat dux Cælesýriæ et Phœnícis:
<n>6</n> Et nuntiávit ei pecúniis innumerabílibus plenum esse ærárium Ierosólymis, et commúnes cópias imménsas esse, quæ non pértinent ad ratiónem sacrificiórum; esse autem possíbile sub potestáte regis cádere univérsa.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> In hymnis et confessiónibus benedicébant Dóminum,
* Qui magna fecit in Israël, et victóriam dedit illis Dóminus omnípotens.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>2 Mac 3:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> But one Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was appointed overseer of the temple, strove in opposition to the high priest, to bring about some unjust thing in the city.
<n>5</n> And when he could not overcome Onias he went to Apollonius the son of Tharseas, who at that time was governor of Celesyria and Phenicia:
<n>6</n> And told him, that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of immense sums of money, and the common store was infinite, which did not belong to the account of the sacrifices: and that it was possible to bring all into the king's hands.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> They praised the Lord with psalms and thanksgiving

<r>℟.</r> Who had done so great things for Israel, and given them the victory the Lord Almighty.

<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, refúgium nostrum et virtus: adésto piis Ecclésiæ tuæ précibus, auctor ipse pietátis, et præsta; ut, quod fidéliter pétimus, efficáciter consequámur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

b.249eb34482:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, our Refuge and Strength, Who art the author of all godliness, be ready, we beseech thee, to hear the devout prayers of thy Church, and grant that those things which we ask faithfully, we may obtain effectually.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.fd0e195a6a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>uodécimo Kaléndas Novémbris Luna vicésima prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Cypro natális sancti Hilariónis Abbátis, cuius vitam, virtútibus atque miráculis plenam, sanctus Hierónymus scripsit.
<h>A</h>pud Colóniam Agrippínam item natális sanctárum Ursulæ et Sociárum eius; quæ, pro Christiána religióne et virginitátis constántia ab Hunnis interféctæ, martýrio vitam consummárunt, earúmque plúrima córpora fuérunt Colóniæ cóndita.
<h>A</h>pud Ostia Tiberína sancti Astérii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui (ut in passióne beáti Callísti Papæ légitur) sub Alexándro Imperatóre passus est.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ natális sanctórum Dásii, Zótici, Caii et aliórum duódecim mílitum; qui, post divérsa torménta, in mare demérsi sunt.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Viatóris, qui éxstitit miníster beáti Iusti, Lugdunénsis Epíscopi.
<h>M</h>aróniæ, prope Antiochíam, in Sýria, sancti Malchi Mónachi.
<h>I</h>n castro Laudunénsi sanctæ Cilíniæ, matris beáti Remígii, Epíscopi Rheménsis.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.1c46c506b4:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 21st 2027, the 21st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, the holy Abbot Hilarion, of whom holy Jerome hath written the life, full of graces and wonders.
<h>A</h>t Cologne, the holy Ursula and her Companions, who, for their steadfastness in Christianity and chastity, were massacred by the Huns, and so closed their earthly life by martyrdom.
<h>V</h>ery many of their bodies are buried at Cologne.
<h>A</h>t Ostia, the holy martyr Asterius, a Priest who suffered under the Emperor Alexander, as is written in the acts of the passion of the blessed Pope Kallistus.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Dasius, Zoticus, Caius, and twelve others, soldiers, who were diversely tormented, and then drowned in the sea, (under the Emperor Diocletian.)
<h>A</h>t Lyon, holy Viator, the servant of the blessed Justus, Bishop of Lyon.
<h>A</h>t Maronia, in Syria, near Antioch, (in the fourth century,) the holy monk Malchus.
<h>A</h>t Laon, holy Cilinia, mother of the blessed Remy, Bishop of Reims.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
